stem: Evaluate the definite integral of (x + 2)^2 with respect to x from x = 1 to x = 4.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Integrating x^2 as x^3 (raising exponent but not dividing by the new exponent 3): F(x) = x^3+2x^2+4x. F(4)-F(1) = (64+32+16)-(1+2+4) = 112-7 = 105.
Integrating every term without dividing by the new exponent: antiderivative of x^2 as x^3 and of 4x as 4x^2 (instead of 2x^2). F(x) = x^3+4x^2+4x. F(4)-F(1) = (64+64+16)-(1+4+4) = 144-9 = 135.
Not expanding; instead applying (x+2)^3 as the antiderivative without dividing by 3 (missing the chain-rule factor): F(x) = (x+2)^3. F(4)-F(1) = 6^3-3^3 = 216-27 = 189.

explanation_sections.punchline: The setup decision is expanding the bracket first, which makes each term integrable by a direct power rule.
explanation_sections.approach: Expand-then-integrate: write (x+2)^2 as x^2+4x+4, apply the power rule to each term (raise exponent by 1, divide by new exponent), then evaluate at both limits and subtract.
explanation_sections.lesson: After raising the exponent from n to n+1 when integrating x^n, you must divide by n+1. Missing this division doubles or triples the result.
explanation_sections.timing: 70-90 seconds. The fraction 64/3 - 1/3 = 63/3 = 21 simplifies cleanly. Do the fractional and integer parts separately to avoid errors.
